title: The hare and the tortoise.
lines: In a green meadow, at the edge of the forest, lived lots of animals.
There was a hare with long ears and strong back legs.
He was the fastest of them all.
And he always let everyone know it.
Nobody is as fast as me!
A tortoise lived in the same meadow.
She had a big, hard shell on her back, and she walked very, very slowly.
The hare always laughed at her.
By the time she gets to the other side of the meadow, it'll be winter!
One day the tortoise said: Hare, shall we have a race?
A race to the big oak tree on the hill?
The hare almost fell over laughing.
I'll win that with my eyes closed!
All the animals came to watch.
In a few seconds he was already far away.
The tortoise took her first little step.
Halfway there the hare looked back.
He couldn't even see the tortoise anymore.
I'll have a little nap in the sun.
He lay down in the soft grass under a tree.
And the hare fell into a deep sleep.
She only looked ahead, at the big oak tree.
She walked past the sleeping hare.
It was hard, but she kept going.
When the hare woke up, the sun had almost gone down.
He jumped up and ran as fast as he could to the hill.
But when he got to the top, he saw something unbelievable.
There, under the big oak tree, stood the tortoise.
You know, you don't have to be the fastest.
If you keep going steadily and don't give up, you'll always get there.
And from that day on the hare never laughed at anyone for being slow again.
